title: GPT from scratch
description: Build a character-level GPT in eight runnable steps: tokenizer, batches, a bigram model that learns, the averaging trick, one attention head, transformer blocks, the full GPT, and generation from the saved model.

steps.title: Turn text into numbers
try: Run it on your own text with --data. How big is your vocabulary?
Write a word-level tokenizer instead (split on spaces). How many tokens does the vocabulary have now, and how long is the encoded text?

steps.title: One chunk of text is many training examples
try: Change --block-size to 3. How many examples does one chunk hold now?
Print a batch from the validation split instead of the training split.

steps.title: A bigram model that learns
try: Try --lr 1 and --lr 1e-4. Which one learns, which one jumps around, which one barely moves?
Before training the loss is about 4.7, above the -ln(1/65) = 4.17 of uniform guessing. Why is a randomly initialised model worse than guessing?
Look at model.token_embedding_table.weight after training: which character is most likely after 'q'?

steps.title: Averaging over the past with a triangular mask
try: Change the scores in version 3 from zeros to random numbers. Do the rows still sum to 1? Is the future still blocked?
Replace torch.tril by torch.ones: what does position 0 now average over?

steps.title: One head of self-attention
try: Run with --no-mask. The loss drops far below 2.4 (to about 0.4), yet the generated text is garbage. Why?
Run with --no-scale and a larger --n-embd 128. What happens to training?
Remove pos_emb from the sum. Can the model still tell 'dog bites man' from 'man bites dog'?

steps.title: Multi-head attention and feed-forward make a block
try: Compare --n-head 1, 4 and 8 at the same --n-embd 32.
Run with --n-layer 4. Is the loss better than with one block? Keep the number for step 7.

steps.title: The complete GPT: residuals, layer norm, dropout
try: Run --preset tiny with and without --no-residual. How much do residual connections help?
Train on your own text with --data. What does the model pick up first: spelling, word lengths, line breaks?
Raise --dropout to 0.3 and compare the gap between train and val loss.

steps.title: Generate text from the trained model
try: Use --explain 10 with --temperature 0.5 and 1.5. How do the probabilities change?
Use --top-k 1. Why does the text start repeating itself?
Give a prompt longer than the context. What does the model actually see?

data.title: Tiny Shakespeare: about 1.1 million characters of Shakespeare's plays
